author: Yffe
content:
External reviewer (human + agent) caught a real gap in the 'no general quantifiers / quantifier-locked SpecTherm' thesis (§4.2/§6). Verdict: partly true, worth fixing; the 'just renamed it' framing overstates it.

WHAT HOLDS: a combinator lowers to a BOUNDED quantifier with a FROZEN trigger on the predicate application (forall_in(s,p) == forall|i| 0<=i<s.len() ==> #[trigger] p(s[i])). Bounded range kills unbounded-quantifier blowup; frozen trigger removes Verus's heuristic trigger-inference variance (a primary SMT-discontinuity source). For a FLAT closure body this genuinely locks instantiation.

THE HOLE (reviewer is right): the closure body is currently UNrestricted and can contain ANOTHER combinator -> nested bounded quantifier -> the composition reintroduces multi-quantifier instantiation interaction. Our loop-3 thermite-spec validator currently ACCEPTS this (its critic tested forall_in(xs, |x| exists_in(ys, |y| y==x)) as valid). So the cage has exactly the described hole.

FIX (a strengthening, not a retreat): restrict SpecTherm closure bodies to a FLAT predicate fragment -- comparisons, arithmetic, boolean ops, field/index, and NAMED spec-fn calls -- but FORBID a nested combinator call inside a combinator's closure. Invariant becomes honest: 'every quantifier is a bounded combinator with a frozen trigger; composition happens only via named spec fns (dec-measured, auditable), never anonymous nested quantifiers.' Enforce as one new reject in the thermite-spec validator (which today over-permits) + clarify §4.2 + .design/spec/spectherm-combinators.md. Corpus is UNAFFECTED (sum/binary_search closures are flat: |x| x != needle etc.). Caveat: a flat closure may still call a named spec fn that internally quantifies -- depth is named+bounded, not zero; we kill anonymous arbitrary nesting, the unpredictable part.

Touches #2 (validator) + the design docs, NOT #5/forge. Could empirically demonstrate the flat-vs-nested distinction in real verus before implementing.
